newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD wants to buy up to 15 pct of Poland's PBK.
newsitem.headline: EBRD wants to buy up to 15 pct of Poland's PBK.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is willing to invest in up to 15 percent of Poland's Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), EBRD press office said on Thursday.
"The board of (EBRD) directors confirmed yesterday its project of investment in PBK...it may be up to 15 percent," an EBRD press officer in London told Reuters over the telephone.
The official declined to give any further details.
Poland is offering up to 65 percent of the Warsaw-based large retail bank in a tender and the final decision on the choice of investors is expected in mid-June.
So far only South Korea's Samsung and a Polish group made up of Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA, Kredyt Bank, Polish Development Bank SA and TUiR Warta insurer have confirmed they were bidding for PBK.

The Polish group has said it wanted to buy at least 51 percent of PBK and some Polish newspapers quoted banking sources as saying that the EBRD might join the group to take an extra 15 percent. EBRD declined to comment on the reports.
